content.user_title: Research Topics Across Web, Docs, and Code
content.value_statement: Research questions often require current web evidence, local documentation, and code examples. This skill coordinates those sources and synthesizes findings with clear confidence labels.
actual_capabilities: Selects quick, standard, or extensive modes based on speed and depth needs.
Coordinates web, documentation, and code researchers in parallel.
Cross-validates findings across source types in standard and extensive modes.
Labels synthesized findings as high, medium, low, or conflicting confidence.
Returns source links, local file references, timing, and agent response metadata.
limitations: Web research requires network connectivity and cannot access paywalled content.
Quick mode uses limited queries and may miss nuanced information.
Extensive mode uses more model calls and can take up to ten minutes.
The referenced synthesis-patterns.md guide is not included in the package.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Technical Approach
use_cases.description: Compare official guidance, local documentation, and implementation examples before selecting a library or architecture.

use_cases.title: Build Evidence-Based Documentation
use_cases.description: Gather current sources, code references, and conflicting viewpoints before drafting technical documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Decision Brief
use_cases.description: Research several options, assess source agreement, and produce an actionable recommendation with evidence gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Fact Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quick mode to verify [claim]. Cite the strongest web and documentation sources, then state one confidence level.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one verified answer.

prompt_templates.title: Standard Technical Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Use standard mode to research [technical topic]. Compare web guidance with local documentation and code examples. Highlight disagreements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs balanced implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Extensive Decision Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extensive mode to compare [option A] and [option B] for [context]. Evaluate architecture, implementation, risks, costs, and source conflicts.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team must make a documented technical decision.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence-Led Research Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [complex question] in extensive mode. Assign distinct source angles, cross-validate every major claim, identify evidence gaps, and recommend further research.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a comprehensive report from varied evidence.

output_examples.input: Quick mode: Is WebSocket authentication part of the initial HTTP handshake?
output_examples.output: WebSocket authentication commonly uses the initial HTTP upgrade request. Confidence: HIGH. Sources include official protocol guidance and matching documentation.

output_examples.input: Standard mode: Research token validation practices for WebSocket services.
output_examples.output: The report compares current guidance with local code patterns. It marks supported findings as HIGH confidence and identifies one unresolved source conflict.

output_examples.input: Extensive mode: Compare two coding assistants for a large engineering team.
output_examples.output: The analysis compares architecture, security, maintenance, workflow, and cost. It recommends one option, cites supporting sources, and lists remaining evidence gaps.

best_practices: Choose the smallest mode that provides enough source coverage.
Give the query a clear scope, date range, and decision context.
Review low-confidence and conflicting findings before using recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a single source as settled evidence.
Do not use extensive mode for simple definitions or routine lookups.
Do not present incomplete results without noting timeouts or missing sources.

faq.question: Which research modes are available?
faq.answer: Quick mode handles simple checks, standard mode supports typical research, and extensive mode provides deeper comparison and synthesis.

faq.question: Which sources can the skill research?
faq.answer: It can search current web content, local documentation, project specifications, implementation files, tests, and configuration examples.

faq.question: How are confidence labels assigned?
faq.answer: High confidence requires at least three agreeing sources. Medium requires two, while low indicates only one supporting source.

faq.question: What happens when web search is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill returns documentation-only results and notes that web evidence was unavailable.

faq.question: Does the skill modify project files?
faq.answer: No. It searches and reads code examples but does not instruct researchers to modify files.

faq.question: How long does extensive mode take?
faq.answer: Extensive mode allows up to ten minutes and uses more model calls than the other modes.
